fixed.q: Which of the following is an input device which can detect the presence or absence of a pencil or pen mark on a paper?
fixed.w: An OMR detects the presence or absence of pencil/pen marks at fixed positions, as in OMR answer sheets.

fixed.q: Which of the following printer is type of impact printer?
fixed.w: Dot-matrix printers strike pins against an inked ribbon, so they are impact printers. Inkjet, laser and thermal printers are non-impact.

fixed.q: Which of the following is frequently used to ensure that data is correctly entered into a computer?
fixed.w: Input controls (validation checks) ensure data is entered correctly.

fixed.q: Which of the following is an example of an output device?
fixed.w: A Visual Display Unit (monitor) is an output device.

fixed.q: Which storage media supports only sequential access?
fixed.w: Magnetic tape supports only sequential access.

fixed.q: The Insert key in a keyboard of a computer system is used to toggle between ______ and ______ modes during data entry.
fixed.w: The Insert key toggles between insert and overwrite (overtype) modes.

fixed.q: Which of the following input devices is used to detect orientation and angular velocity?
fixed.w: A gyroscope senses orientation and angular velocity.

fixed.q: Which of the following statement(s) is/are not true about magnetic tapes? I. Direct access device II. Store large volume of data III. Use for backup purpose
fixed.w: Magnetic tape is a sequential-access device, so only I is false. It does store large volumes and is used for backup.

fixed.q: Which of the following is a impact printer?
fixed.w: A dot-matrix printer is an impact printer.

fixed.q: Which input device is used for reading answer to question in a test or survey?
fixed.w: OMR reads marked answers on test or survey sheets.

fixed.q: The ability to input data directly into a computer system by speaking to it is known as ______.
fixed.w: Speech recognition converts spoken words into computer input.

fixed.q: Data entry cannot be done by which of the following?
fixed.w: COM (Computer Output on Microfilm) is an output technique. OCR, OMR, MICR and voice recognition are all input methods.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: Magnetic tape can act as an input medium.
Magnetic tape can act as an output medium.
Magnetic tape can act as a secondary storage medium.
fixed.w: Tape can be read (input), written (output) and used for backup storage, so all three are true.

fixed.q: ______ are a set of computer programs with necessary documentation.
fixed.w: Software packages are programs together with their documentation.

fixed.q: Which of the following computer programs provides instructions for computer operations?
fixed.w: System software provides the instructions that operate the computer.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: CMOS chip is powered by the battery located in the mother board.
POST is the process performed by BIOS immediately after the system is shutdown.
The bootstrap program is stored in RAM.
BIOS was developed by Charles Babbage.
fixed.w: The CMOS chip that stores BIOS settings is powered by a coin battery on the motherboard. POST runs at power-on, the bootstrap is in ROM, and BIOS was not Babbage's.

fixed.q: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
o: 5 kilobytes is equal to 10,240 half bytes
fixed.w: 4 KB = 4096 bytes, not 4069. The others are correct: 5 KB = 10,240 nibbles, 3 KB = 24,576 bits, 2 KB = 4096 nibbles.

fixed.q: Which of the following is NOT true about software?
o: System software is written in a high-level language.
Application software is written in a high-level language.
System software plays a vital role for the effective functioning of a system.
System software is written in a low-level language.
fixed.w: As per the official key: system software is typically written in low-level or system languages, so 'written in a high-level language' is marked not true.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) A compiler translates the entire source code line by line. ii) Computer architecture refers to those attributes of a system visible to a programmer. iii) The RISC computer organisation reduces the cycles per instruction at the cost of the number of instructions per program to increase CPU performance. iv) All the arithmetic and logical processing is performed by the Arithmetic Logic Unit under the supervision of a control unit.
fixed.w: A compiler translates the whole program at once, not line by line, so i is false; ii, iii and iv are true.

fixed.q: Due to which property a computer can work for hours without creating any error and without grumbling?
fixed.w: Diligence: a computer can work for hours without tiredness, loss of concentration or errors.

fixed.q: ______ is a controlled electronic switch fabricated using a semiconductor.
fixed.w: A transistor is a semiconductor device used as a controlled electronic switch or amplifier.

fixed.q: 1 picosecond = ______
fixed.w: Pico = 10⁻¹², so 1 ps = 10⁻¹² s.

fixed.q: Computer output displayed on the screen without a permanent copy is called
fixed.w: On-screen output is a soft copy. Printed output is a hard copy.

fixed.q: The set of computer programs, procedures and associated documents related to the effective operation of a computer system is referred to as
fixed.w: This is the standard definition of software: programs plus procedures plus documentation.

fixed.q: Which of the following is an accounting application software?
fixed.w: Tally is accounting software.

fixed.q: Which is the shortcut key to find and replace action in MS-Word?
fixed.w: Ctrl+H opens Find and Replace in MS Word.

fixed.q: What does the VLOOKUP function do?
o: Checks whether text is the same in one cell as in the next
fixed.w: VLOOKUP finds a value in the first column and returns related data from the same row, i.e. related records.

fixed.q: Which of the following is an absolute cell reference?
fixed.w: `$B$1` is an absolute reference (both column and row fixed).

fixed.q: Which of the following formulas will Excel not be able to calculate?
fixed.w: (10 − 10) = 0, so the formula divides by zero and gives #DIV/0!.

fixed.q: Which of the following is not a valid formula in MS Excel?
fixed.w: Excel has AVERAGE(), not AVG().

fixed.q: To add two cells (A1 and A2) together you use the following formula
fixed.w: =A1+A2 adds two cells.

fixed.q: Which phenomenon causes a phase shift in the retardation plates?
fixed.w: Retardation (wave) plates shift phase through double refraction (birefringence): the o- and e-rays travel at different speeds.

fixed.q: Which transition generates laser output in the CO₂ molecule?
fixed.w: The CO₂ laser works on transitions between vibrational (vibrational–rotational) energy states.

fixed.q: What is the lifetime of an atom's ground state in stimulated absorption?
fixed.w: In stimulated absorption, an unexcited atom stays in its stable ground state indefinitely, so its lifetime is infinite.

fixed.q: Does polarisation vary with direction?
fixed.w: 'transverse wave': polarisation is a property of transverse waves, whose vibration direction is perpendicular to propagation.

fixed.q: Which of the following effects is the phenomenon of emission of electrons from the surfaces of certain substances, mainly metals, when light of a shorter wavelength is incident upon them?
fixed.w: Emission of electrons under light of short wavelength is the photoelectric effect.

fixed.q:
Match the system with the respective unit to represent heat.
Systems: (a) CGS; (b) FPS; (c) SI

Units: (i) BTU; (ii) Joule; (iii) Calorie
fixed.w: CGS uses the calorie, FPS uses the BTU and SI uses the joule.

fixed.q: A body of mass 4.9 kg hangs from a spring and oscillates with a period of 0.6 sec. How much will the spring shorten when the body is removed?
fixed.w: The static extension x = mg/k = gT²/4π² = 9.8 × 0.36/39.48 ≈ 0.089 m.

fixed.q: An LED emits green light of wavelength λ = 5511.11 Å. Find the value of Eg.
The refractive index of the core of an optical fibre is greater than that of the cladding because:
o: the light gets totally internally reflected into the core
the light gets reflected at the entrance end of the optical fibre
the light gets restricted at the entrance end of the optical fibre
the light gets refracted into cladding
fixed.w: A higher-index core lets light undergo total internal reflection and stay in the core.

fixed.q: Which of the following is/are associated with turbulent flow? i) Flow of liquid is orderly. ii) Flow of liquid is zigzag and random.
fixed.w: Turbulent flow is zigzag and random; orderly flow is laminar.

fixed.q:
Match the column 'Moduli of elasticity' with the column 'Descriptions'.
Moduli: a) Young's modulus; b) Bulk (or) Volume modulus; c) Shearing (or) Rigidity modulus

Descriptions: i) Ratio of the shearing stress applied to the body to the shearing strain produced; ii) Ratio of linear stress to linear strain; iii) Ratio of bulk stress to bulk strain.
fixed.w: Young's = linear stress/strain (ii), Bulk = bulk stress/strain (iii), Rigidity = shear stress/strain (i).

fixed.q: Which of the following correctly defines coplanar forces?
o: When the lines of action of all forces lie in one plane.
Two or more than two forces acting at a point.
A single force, which acting along with other forces, keeps the body in equilibrium.
A single force which produces the same effect as that produced by two or more forces acting on the body.
fixed.w: Coplanar forces have lines of action lying in one plane.

fixed.q: Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements? i) Physical quantities which have magnitude only are called scalar quantities. ii) Physical quantities which have both magnitude and direction are called vector quantities. iii) Two equal and opposite parallel forces acting at different points in a body constitute a couple.
fixed.w: All three are standard definitions: scalar, vector and couple.

fixed.q: Which of the following is correct regarding electric power?
fixed.w: Electric power P = VI (= I²R = V²/R).

fixed.q: Linearity error is expressed as a percentage of ______.
fixed.w: Linearity error (of a DAC/ADC) is expressed as a percentage of the full-scale, i.e. maximum, output voltage.

fixed.q: According to ______ law, the force between two charges is directly proportional to the product of theirs charges.
fixed.w: Coulomb's law: F = k·q₁q₂/r², proportional to the product of the charges.

fixed.q: 1 KB (kilobyte) equals:
fixed.w: In computing, 1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB, 1 TB = 1024 GB.

fixed.q: A nibble is:
fixed.w: A nibble is 4 bits (half a byte); a byte is 8 bits.

fixed.q: Integrated circuits (ICs) were used in which generation of computers?
fixed.w: 1st: vacuum tubes. 2nd: transistors. 3rd: ICs. 4th: microprocessors (VLSI). 5th: AI, ULSI.

fixed.q: The first general-purpose electronic digital computer was:
fixed.w: ENIAC (1946) used vacuum tubes. UNIVAC was the first commercial computer in the USA. PARAM is India's supercomputer series.

fixed.q: Which software controls and manages the computer hardware?
fixed.w: The OS is system software that manages hardware and gives services to applications.

fixed.q: A program that converts a whole high-level program into machine code at once is a:
fixed.w: A compiler translates the whole program at once. An interpreter translates line by line. An assembler converts assembly into machine code.

fixed.q: Which of these is a volatile memory?
fixed.w: RAM loses its contents when power is off. ROM, flash and disks are non-volatile.

fixed.q: The fastest memory in a computer is:
fixed.w: Speed order: registers > cache > main memory (RAM) > secondary storage.

fixed.q: MICR technology is mainly used by:
fixed.w: MICR (magnetic ink character recognition) reads the magnetic-ink characters on cheques. OMR reads marks on answer sheets.

fixed.q: Which device is both an input and an output device?
fixed.w: A touch screen takes touch input and shows output.

fixed.q: The resolution of a printer is measured in:
fixed.w: DPI measures print resolution. PPM (pages per minute) measures print speed.

fixed.q: In MS Word, the shortcut to make text bold is:
fixed.w: Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+I italic, Ctrl+U underline, Ctrl+E centre, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo.

fixed.q: In MS Excel, every formula begins with:
fixed.w: Excel formulas start with =, e.g. =SUM(A1:A5).

fixed.q: In MS Excel, the intersection of a row and a column is a:
fixed.w: A cell is identified by its column letter and row number, e.g. B3.

fixed.q: The shortcut to start a slide show from the first slide in PowerPoint is:
fixed.w: F5 starts from the beginning; Shift+F5 starts from the current slide. F7 is spell check and F12 is Save As.

fixed.q: Ohm's law states that (at constant temperature):
fixed.w: Voltage across a conductor is proportional to current: V = IR.

fixed.q: An n-type semiconductor is made by doping silicon with a:
fixed.w: Pentavalent donors give extra electrons (n-type). Trivalent acceptors create holes (p-type).

fixed.q: A p–n junction diode conducts readily when it is:
fixed.w: Forward bias (p to +, n to −) reduces the depletion barrier; reverse bias widens it.

fixed.q: The SI unit of force is the:
fixed.w: Newton = kg·m/s². Joule is energy, pascal is pressure, watt is power.

fixed.q: The speed of light in vacuum is about:
Total internal reflection occurs when light goes from:
o: A denser to a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle
A rarer to a denser medium at any angle
A denser to a rarer medium at an angle less than the critical angle
fixed.w: This is the principle behind optical fibres (core index > cladding index).

fixed.q: LASER stands for:
o: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Light Absorption by Stimulated Emission of Rays
Light Amplification by Spontaneous Emission of Radiation
fixed.w: Lasing needs population inversion and stimulated emission.

fixed.q: The charge on an electron is about:
fixed.w: e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg is the electron mass; 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s is Planck's constant.

fixed.q: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω in series have a total resistance of:
fixed.w: Series resistances add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω. In parallel, reciprocals add.

fixed.q: The frequency of a wave with time period 0.02 s is:
fixed.w: f = 1/T = 1/0.02 = 50 Hz (Indian mains frequency).

fixed.q: A laser needs more atoms in the excited state than in the lower state. This condition is:
fixed.w: It is produced by pumping (optical, electrical, etc.).

fixed.q: Laser light is:
fixed.w: Coherent means the waves keep a constant phase relation.

fixed.q: Emission of electrons from a metal when light of suitable frequency falls on it is the:
fixed.w: Einstein: hν = work function + kinetic energy of the electron.

fixed.q: The photon energy is given by:
Optical fibres work on the principle of:
fixed.w: The core has a higher refractive index than the cladding.

fixed.q: Light waves are transverse. This is proved by:
fixed.w: Longitudinal waves (such as sound) cannot be polarised.

fixed.q: In an intrinsic semiconductor, adding a pentavalent impurity (e.g. phosphorus) makes it:
fixed.w: Trivalent impurities (boron) make it p-type, with holes as majority carriers.

fixed.q: An LED emits light when its p–n junction is:
fixed.w: Photon energy ≈ band gap: Eg (eV) ≈ 1240 / λ (nm).

fixed.q: The SI unit of heat is the ___ and the CGS unit is the ___.
fixed.w: 1 calorie ≈ 4.186 J. The BTU is the FPS unit.

fixed.q: The period of a mass–spring system is:
fixed.w: For a simple pendulum, T = 2π√(l/g).

fixed.q: Doppler effect is the apparent change in ___ due to relative motion of source and observer.
fixed.w: A higher pitch is heard as the source approaches.

fixed.q: Which is a non-volatile storage device?
fixed.w: Volatile memory loses its data when power is off.

fixed.q: Which device reads pencil marks on answer sheets?
fixed.w: OCR reads printed text; MICR reads magnetic-ink characters on cheques.

fixed.q: Which printer is an impact printer?
fixed.w: Impact printers strike an inked ribbon.

fixed.q: Screen resolution 1920 × 1080 refers to the number of:
fixed.w: Pixels across × pixels down.

fixed.q: Which has the fastest access time?
fixed.w: Hierarchy: registers > cache > RAM > SSD > HDD > tape.

fixed.q: 1 KB equals:
A Blu-ray disc uses a ___ laser.
fixed.w: CDs use infrared, DVDs red, Blu-ray blue-violet; the shorter wavelength allows more data.

fixed.q: Who is known as the father of the computer?
fixed.w: He designed the Analytical Engine. Ada Lovelace is called the first programmer.

fixed.q: Computers of the first generation used:
fixed.w: Second generation: transistors; third: ICs; fourth: microprocessors (VLSI); fifth: AI/ULSI.

fixed.q: The brain of the computer is the:
fixed.w: The CPU contains the ALU, the control unit and registers.

fixed.q: Software that controls the hardware and provides a platform for applications is:
fixed.w: MS Word is application software.

fixed.q: A program that translates an entire high-level program at once into machine code is a:
fixed.w: An interpreter translates line by line; an assembler translates assembly language.

fixed.q: Which is an example of open-source software?
fixed.w: Its source code is freely available to modify.

fixed.q: In MS Word, Ctrl + Z does:
fixed.w: Ctrl + Y = redo; Ctrl + X = cut; Ctrl + B = bold.

fixed.q: In Excel, $A$1 is a(n) ___ reference.
fixed.w: $A1 and A$1 are mixed references.

fixed.q: Which Excel function returns the number of cells that contain numbers?
fixed.w: COUNTA counts non-empty cells; COUNTIF counts with a condition.

fixed.q: In PowerPoint, F5 starts:
o: The slide show from the beginning
fixed.w: Shift + F5 starts from the current slide.

fixed.q: In MS Word, Mail Merge is used to:
o: Create personalised letters for many recipients
fixed.w: It combines a main document with a data source.

theory.Basics & terminology:
• Generations: 1st vacuum tubes (ENIAC, UNIVAC), 2nd transistors, 3rd ICs, 4th microprocessors (VLSI), 5th AI (ULSI).
• Units: bit, nibble (4 bits), byte (8 bits); KB = 1024 B, MB, GB, TB, PB.
• Software: system (OS, utilities, translators) vs application. Translators: compiler (whole program), interpreter (line by line), assembler.
• Languages: machine (1GL), assembly (2GL), high-level (3GL), 4GL (SQL), 5GL (Prolog, AI).
theory.Input/output devices & storage:
• Input: keyboard, mouse, scanner, OMR (answer sheets), OCR (text), MICR (cheques), barcode reader, light pen, joystick. Output: monitor, printer, plotter, speaker. Both: touch screen.
• Printers: impact (dot-matrix, daisy wheel) vs non-impact (laser, inkjet); resolution in DPI, speed in PPM/CPS.
• Memory: registers > cache > RAM (volatile; SRAM for cache, DRAM main) > secondary. ROM types: PROM, EPROM (UV), EEPROM (electrical), flash.
• Storage: HDD (magnetic), SSD (flash), CD/DVD/Blu-ray (optical).
theory.MS Office:
• Word: Ctrl+B bold, I italic, U underline, E centre, L left, R right, J justify, Z undo, Y redo, F7 spelling, Ctrl+Enter page break.
• Excel: formulas start with =; cell = column letter + row number; $A$1 absolute reference; functions SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, IF, VLOOKUP; .xlsx.
• PowerPoint: F5 from the beginning, Shift+F5 from the current slide; slide sorter view; .pptx.
• F12 Save As, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print.
theory.Physics:
• Photoelectric effect: electrons emitted by light (Einstein). E (eV) = 12400/λ(Å), so 5511 Å → 2.25 eV.
• Optical fibre: core refractive index > cladding → total internal reflection.
• Laser: CO₂ laser uses vibrational transitions; ground state lifetime is infinite.
• Polarisation shows that light is a transverse wave; retardation plates work by double refraction.
• Coulomb's law: F ∝ q₁q₂/r². P = VI. Spring: T = 2π√(m/k).
• Moduli: Young's (longitudinal), bulk (volume), rigidity/shear (shape).
